text: Tülay Adalı is a Distinguished University Professor of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County, with research interests in signal processing, machine learning, and data fusion. She co-authored the book Adaptive Signal Processing: Next Generation Solutions (Wiley, 2010) with Simon Haykin and Blind Identification and Separation of Complex-valued Signals (Wiley, 2013) with Eric Moreau. In 2008, she was elected a Fellow of the American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering "for outstanding research, mentorship, and leadership in the field of biomedical imaging and signal processing," and in 2009, she became a Fellow of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers "For contributions to nonlinear and complex-valued statistical signal processing." She served as an IEEE Signal Processing Society Distinguished Lecturer from 2012 to 2013 and was named a Fulbright Scholar in 2015. She is the sister of computer scientist Sibel Adalı.
